newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW has small deficit in 9-mths to Mch.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW has small deficit in 9-mths to Mch.

text.p: The New South Wales state government recorded an underlying budget deficit of A$6 million for the nine months to March 1997, NSW Treasurer Michael Egan said.
This compared with a A$153 million surplus for the same period last year, he said in statement.
The 1997/98 state budget released on May 6 said the final budget result for the 1996/97 fiscal year ending June 30 is projected to be a surplus of A$67 million.
The financial result on a headline basis in the nine month period was a deficit of A$46 million compared with a surplus of A$145 million for the same period last year.
This comprises a surplus of A$1.336 billion on the current account and a deficit of A$1.382 billion on the capital account.

The turnaround in the March result between last year and this year is predominantly due to an increase in the level of departmental payments, particurlarly in the health and education sectors, offset in part by increased revenue from taxes, fees and fines, the government statement added.
